title: Does the EU Machinery Regulation require operator training?
description: Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 applies from 20 January 2027: what its instructions rules require of manufacturers, and where operator training duties sit.
shortAnswer: Not directly. Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 on machinery, which applies from 20 January 2027, places information duties on manufacturers: instructions for use must indicate whether particular training is required and, where necessary, include instructions for training operators. The duty to actually train workers who use machinery sits with employers under Directive 2009/104/EC on work equipment, which requires adequate training on the risks of use. The two instruments work together.
keyTakeaways: Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 applies from 20 January 2027 and repeals Directive 2006/42/EC from that date; products placed on the market under the directive before then may still be made available.

Annex III section 1.1.2(b)(iii) requires the manufacturer to inform users of residual risks, indicate whether any particular training is required and specify any need for personal protective equipment.
Annex III section 1.7.4.2(1)(k) requires instructions for putting into service and use and, if necessary, instructions for the training of operators.
Article 10(7) allows digital instructions, which must stay accessible online for the expected lifetime of the product and at least 10 years, with paper copies free on request within one month.

The Machinery Regulation does not oblige employers to train anyone; Article 9 of Directive 2009/104/EC requires employers to ensure workers using work equipment receive adequate training, including on the risks.
jurisdiction: European Union (all Member States; directly applicable regulation with EEA relevance, applying from 20 January 2027)
regulator: European Commission under Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, enforced by Member State market surveillance authorities; employer duties under Directive 2009/104/EC enforced by national labor inspectorates
appliesTo: Manufacturers of machinery and related products placed on the EU market
Importers and distributors, who must ensure instructions accompany products
Employers using machinery as work equipment, through Directive 2009/104/EC
Training and technical documentation teams that turn manufacturer instructions into operator training

sections.heading: What is and is not a training duty under Regulation (EU) 2023/1230?

blocks.text: [Regulation (EU) 2023/1230](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02023R1230-20260727) is a product safety law. It sets essential health and safety requirements that machinery must meet before it is placed on the market, and its obligations fall on manufacturers, authorized representatives, importers and distributors. It does not contain an obligation on employers or operators to train people.

blocks.text: In practice the regulation shapes training indirectly. The manufacturer's statement that particular training is required, and any operator training instructions, become key inputs to the employer's own training under work equipment and [OSH framework](/regulations/eu-osh-framework-directive-training) rules.

sections.heading: When does the Machinery Regulation apply?

blocks.text: The regulation applies from 20 January 2027 under Article 54, with some provisions applying earlier. As at November 2026 the main obligations, including the Annex III requirements on instructions, have not yet started to apply.

items: **20 January 2027:** general application; Directive 2006/42/EC is repealed with effect from the same date (Article 51(2)).

**Earlier dates:** Articles 26 to 42 on notified bodies applied from 20 January 2024; Article 50(1) on penalties from 20 October 2026, the date by which Member States had to notify their penalty rules (Article 50(2)).

**Transition:** Member States may not impede the making available of products placed on the market in conformity with Directive 2006/42/EC before 20 January 2027 (Article 52(1)). Machinery bought shortly after that date may therefore come with instructions drafted under the directive.

**Amendments:** the consolidated text of 27 July 2026 incorporates Regulation (EU) 2024/2748 and Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. The latter allows the Commission to add requirements for high-risk AI systems by delegated acts that are to apply by 2 August 2028.

sections.heading: Where does Annex III mention training?

blocks.text: Annex III mentions training in two places, both as information the manufacturer must give. The first is the principle of safety integration in section 1.1.2(b), which sets the order of protective measures: eliminate hazards or minimize risks by design, then take protective measures for risks that cannot be eliminated, and finally "inform users of the residual risks due to any shortcomings of the protective measures adopted, indicate whether any particular training is required and specify any need to provide personal protective equipment."

The second is the list of instruction contents in section 1.7.4.2(1), which includes at point (k) "instructions for the putting into service and use of the machinery or related product and, if necessary, instructions for the training of operators". Under the regulation's general rules, the principles of safety integration in 1.1.2 and the instructions requirements in 1.7.4 apply in all cases, not only where a corresponding hazard exists.

blocks.title: Training is the last line, not the first
blocks.text: Because 1.1.2(b) ranks information and training after inherently safe design and protective measures, a manufacturer cannot rely on operator training to address a risk it could have designed out. The same hierarchy is a useful check for employers: training should cover the residual risks the manufacturer identified, not compensate for missing guards.

sections.heading: Which parts of the instructions matter most for operator training?

blocks.text: Section 1.7.4.2(1) lists the minimum contents of the instructions for use, where applicable. Several points are direct inputs to an operator or maintenance training program:

blocks.text: Section 1.7.4.1 requires the contents to cover reasonably foreseeable misuse, and for machinery intended for non-professional operators, wording and layout must reflect the level of general education and acumen that can reasonably be expected. Maintenance instructions for specialized personnel mandated by the manufacturer may be supplied in a single EU official language those personnel understand (1.7.4).

sections.heading: Can instructions be digital, and what does that mean for training?

blocks.text: Yes. Article 10(7) allows instructions for use in digital format, subject to conditions that matter for anyone building training from them.

items: The product, packaging or an accompanying document must show how to access the digital instructions.
They must be printable, downloadable and savable, so the user can access them at all times, including during a breakdown, and this applies where instructions are embedded in software.
They must be accessible online during the expected lifetime of the product and for at least 10 years after placing on the market.
On request at the time of purchase, the manufacturer must provide paper instructions free of charge within one month.
Safety information essential for putting into service and safe use must be supplied on paper for products intended for, or reasonably likely to be used by, non-professional users.
Instructions must be in a language easily understood by users, as determined by the Member State concerned.

blocks.text: Because manufacturers may update digital instructions, employers should record which version of the instructions each training course was built from. That supports [version control for training content](/guides/how-to-maintain-version-control-for-training-content) and makes later updates traceable.

sections.heading: Where does the employer's duty to train machine operators come from?

blocks.text: The employer's duty comes from EU occupational safety and health law, chiefly [Directive 2009/104/EC](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32009L0104) on the use of work equipment. Article 9 requires the employer to ensure that "workers given the task of using work equipment receive adequate training, including training on any risks which such use may entail", and that workers designated under its Article 6(b) to carry out repairs, modifications, maintenance or servicing of equipment involving a specific risk receive adequate specific training.

Article 8 of the same directive requires the employer to give workers adequate information and, where appropriate, written instructions on the work equipment, covering conditions of use, foreseeable abnormal situations and conclusions from experience, in a form comprehensible to the workers concerned. Both articles apply without prejudice to the training and information duties in Directive 89/391/EEC.

Any national license or certificate required to operate a particular type of machinery sits alongside, not inside, the Machinery Regulation, and should be captured when [mapping training to compliance obligations](/guides/how-to-map-training-to-compliance-obligations).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry converts a manufacturer's instructions for use into a structured framework of tasks, residual risks and required behaviors, each traced to the relevant 1.7.4.2 point and to the instruction version. When the manufacturer revises the digital instructions, the affected knowledge points and the employer's training built on them can be identified directly.

faqs.q: Does the Machinery Regulation require operators to hold a certificate?
faqs.a: No. Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 regulates products and the information supplied with them. It does not create operator certificates or licenses. Any certificate for a particular type of machinery comes from national law, and the general duty to train comes from Directive 2009/104/EC and the OSH framework.

faqs.q: Must manufacturers provide training courses with their machines?
faqs.a: The regulation requires information, not courses. Under Annex III, the manufacturer must indicate whether any particular training is required and, if necessary, include instructions for the training of operators in the instructions for use. Whether training is delivered by the manufacturer, a third party or the employer is a commercial and employer decision.

faqs.q: What changes for training teams on 20 January 2027?
faqs.a: New machinery placed on the market from that date must come with instructions meeting Annex III of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, including the digital format rules in Article 10(7). Products already placed on the market under Directive 2006/42/EC may still be made available, so training teams will handle both formats for some time.

faqs.q: Are digital instructions enough for training on the shop floor?
faqs.a: Digital instructions are allowed if they are printable, downloadable and accessible at all times, including during a breakdown, and users may request paper copies at purchase. The employer must still make information comprehensible to workers under Article 8 of Directive 2009/104/EC, which may mean shorter work instructions derived from the manual.
